knowledge-base.overview: Framework guardrails, patterns, and best practices for Flask 3.0+. Loaded automatically when agents work on Flask projects. Applies to REST APIs, microservices, and server-rendered web applications using Python 3.10+.

core-principles.principle: Always use the factory pattern (create_app()). Never use a global app = Flask(__name__) at module level — it prevents testing and multi-config deployments.
Organize routes into blueprints registered in the factory. Each resource (users, auth, products) gets its own blueprint.
Business logic goes in services (no Flask imports). Endpoints only handle HTTP: parse request, call service, return response.
All Flask extension instances live in extensions.py. Initialize with init_app(app) in the factory.
Use Marshmallow schemas for all serialization and validation. Never trust raw request.json without schema validation.

good-fit.item: Flexibility to choose your own ORM, auth, etc.

consider-alternatives.item: Async support needed (use FastAPI or Quart)

guardrail.rule: Never use a global app = Flask(__name__) at module level. Always use the application factory pattern (create_app()).
guardrail.bad: # app.py — global instance, cannot be tested with different configs app = Flask(__name__) db = SQLAlchemy(app)
guardrail.good: # app/__init__.py — factory pattern def create_app(config_name: str = "development") -> Flask: app = Flask(__name__) app.config.from_object(config[config_name]) db.init_app(app) return app

guardrail.rule: Never store plaintext passwords. Always hash with werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash before saving.
Never use environment variables with fallback secrets in production. Use os.environ["SECRET_KEY"] (raises KeyError) not os.getenv("SECRET_KEY", "fallback").
guardrail.bad: class ProductionConfig(Config): SECRET_KEY = os.getenv("SECRET_KEY", "change-in-production") # fallback leaks
guardrail.good: class ProductionConfig(Config): SECRET_KEY = os.environ["SECRET_KEY"] # raises KeyError if missing

guardrail.rule: Validate all user input with Marshmallow schemas before processing. Never access request.json fields without schema validation.
Register error handlers for all error types in the factory via register_error_handlers(). Never let unhandled exceptions return HTML 500 from a JSON API.
Use Flask-Migrate (Alembic) for all schema changes. Never modify the database schema manually in production.
Configure CORS restrictively in production. Never use CORS_ORIGINS="*" in production configuration.
Set secure cookie options in production: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY, SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE.
Use Flask-JWT-Extended for authentication. Never implement custom JWT parsing by hand.
Use SQLAlchemy ORM for all database access. Never use raw SQL string concatenation.

directory.purpose: All Flask extension instances (db, migrate, ma, jwt, cors)

project-structure.note: app/__init__.py contains create_app() only. app/services/ has no Flask imports. app/schemas/ holds Marshmallow validation.

pattern.name: Application Factory
pattern.description: The factory creates and configures the app, registers extensions and blueprints, and sets up error handlers.

pattern.name: Configuration Classes
Extensions File
pattern.example:
"""Flask extensions initialization.""" from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy from flask_migrate import Migrate from flask_marshmallow import Marshmallow from flask_jwt_extended import JWTManager from flask_cors import CORS
db = SQLAlchemy() migrate = Migrate() ma = Marshmallow() jwt = JWTManager() cors = CORS()

pattern.name: Blueprint Registration
pattern.description: Each resource gets its own blueprint. Import routes inside the blueprint init to register them without circular imports.
pattern.example:
"""API blueprint registration.""" from flask import Blueprint
api_bp = Blueprint("api", __name__)
# Import routes to register them with the blueprint from app.api import users, auth # noqa: F401, E402

pattern.name: Custom Exception Hierarchy and Error Handlers
Jinja2 Template Base
pattern.description: Use template inheritance for server-rendered pages. Jinja2 autoescape is on by default — never disable it.

pattern.name: CLI Commands
pattern.example:
"""Custom CLI commands.""" import click from flask.cli import with_appcontext from app.extensions import db
@click.command("seed-db") @with_appcontext def seed_db(): """Seed database with initial data.""" # Create initial records db.session.commit() click.echo("Database seeded.")

rules.rule: Use pytest with Flask test client
Use fixtures for test data and app context
Test both success and error cases for every endpoint
Mock external services; never call real APIs in tests

knowledge-base.commands:
# Set environment variables export FLASK_APP=run.py export FLASK_ENV=development
# Initialize and run migrations flask db init flask db migrate -m "Initial migration" flask db upgrade
# Seed database flask seed-db
# Run development server flask run
# Run with Gunicorn (production) gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:5000 "app:create_app('production')"
# Run tests pytest pytest -v --cov=app --cov-report=html
# Lint and format ruff check . mypy app/

quick-reference.item: Always create_app(); never global app = Flask(__name__)
All instances in extensions.py; init_app(app) in factory
Business logic in services/; no Flask imports in service files
Marshmallow schemas for all input/output; never raw request.json
Custom AppError hierarchy; register_error_handlers() in factory
os.environ["KEY"] in production (raises on missing); never fallback strings
Flask-Migrate (Alembic) for all schema changes; never manual DDL
